gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 10 build step is the narrowest honest place to keep the virtio_ring survey reviewable without claiming a transport implementation.

The existing virtio core lab slice already covers status negotiation, bounded queue callback bookkeeping, descriptor-shape metadata, and notification accounting, so the ring survey should build on that real foothold instead of pretending those core-side capabilities are still missing.

A dedicated survey gate keeps the live roadmap gap explicit and reviewable now that the repo has both the core slice and the first ring-local helper, so the lane can track the remaining in-memory queue behavior honestly.
The lane needs a Phase 10 note that records the current queue-wrapper gap against the roadmap and prevents the repo from overstating virtio_ring progress.

The first honest virtio_ring step is now landed as a tiny in-memory helper for queue index, descriptor count, split or packed layout metadata, and notification bookkeeping that mirrors only the smallest reviewable shape from virtio_ring.c.

The live ring slice now adds a tiny in-memory used-buffer polling helper that reports only newly consumed chains since the previous poll, which keeps queue-lifecycle review moving without claiming interrupts, DMA, or real descriptor memory.

The live ring slice now adds a tiny callback re-enable helper that flips queue-local callback state back on and reports whether already-consumed chains still need a follow-up poll before any interrupt-facing work is claimed.

The live ring slice now also adds a bounded delayed-callback helper that mirrors the `virtqueue_enable_cb_delayed()` threshold shape while staying queue-local and in memory only before any MMIO register-window work.

The ring survey now records that the tiny in-memory MMIO register-window helper already landed, so the queue-wrapper packet can point at that real transport foothold without pretending it is still only the next proposed step.

With the bounded MMIO register-window helper already landed, interrupt acknowledgement, queue discovery, reset flows, and probe or remove lifecycle behavior remain the still-blocked transport-facing follow-up.
A dedicated slice note keeps the new lab helper honest about what is implemented and what still remains blocked in drivers/virtio/virtio_ring.c work.
